subject: Human Body
title: Memory Cells: The Long Game
description: Learn Memory Cells: The Long Game in one minute.

hook.text: After defeating an infection, your body saves a blueprint. Memory cells sleep for decades, ready to wake instantly.

buildup.text: Memory B cells remember how to make specific antibodies. Memory T cells remember how to kill specific invaders.

discovery.text: When the same pathogen returns, memory cells multiply in hours, not days.

twist.text: Some memory cells last a lifetime. Smallpox vaccination from childhood still protects people in their 80s.

climax.text: Memory cells are the reason you rarely catch the same illness twice. Your body learns and never forgets.

punchline.text: Beat a germ once. Your body remembers it for decades.

quiz.question: What do memory cells do when the same pathogen returns?
options: They die and are replaced by new cells
They multiply rapidly to crush the infection in hours
They send signals to the brain to cause fever
